paragraphs.source_en: On the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month in the fourteenth year of Tenshō, Tokugawa Ieyasu went to Osaka Castle and formally met Toyotomi Hideyoshi.

units.source_en: On the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month in the fourteenth year of Tenshō, Tokugawa Ieyasu went to Osaka Castle and formally met Toyotomi Hideyoshi.
units.source_zh: 德川家康于天正十四年十月二十七赴大坂城，正式和丰臣秀吉见面。

paragraphs.source_zh: “你是何意？”

paragraphs.source_en: “I have brought my troops to the capital precisely to tell His Lordship the Kampaku that henceforth, you need never wear a battle surcoat again.”

paragraphs.source_en: Hideyoshi and Ieyasu played their parts so flawlessly that every onlooker took the performance for truth. Shintarō alone knew the truth, yet even he now held his breath despite himself, overwhelmed by Hideyoshi. Naturally, everyone present was deeply moved: this was no easier than conquering the realm!

units.source_en: Hideyoshi and Ieyasu played their parts so flawlessly that every onlooker took the performance for truth.
units.source_zh: 秀吉与家康的双簧天衣无缝，观者无不信以为真。

units.source_en: Shintarō alone knew the truth, yet even he now held his breath despite himself, overwhelmed by Hideyoshi.
units.source_zh: 知道真相的唯新太郎一人，可此时连他都情不自禁地屏住了呼吸，秀吉令他折服。

units.source_en: Naturally, everyone present was deeply moved: this was no easier than conquering the realm!
units.source_zh: 当然，在座诸人莫不为此感慨良多：这并不比取天下易啊！

paragraphs.source_zh: 秀吉与家康的双簧天衣无缝，观者无不信以为真。知道真相的唯新太郎一人，可此时连他都情不自禁地屏住了呼吸，秀吉令他折服。当然，在座诸人莫不为此感慨良多：这并不比取天下易啊！

paragraphs.source_en: Had Hideyoshi decided not to mention Honda Sakuzaemon after all? Would Ieyasu speak in Sakuzaemon’s defense? Would Ishikawa Kazumasa appear before Ieyasu? Though Ieyasu and Hideyoshi appeared to have made peace, did they truly trust each other from the heart? Shintarō longed to discover the answers to these questions. Meanwhile, the scale of Osaka Castle, Hideyoshi’s magnificence, and the grandeur of the keep opened the young man’s eyes to an entirely new world.

paragraphs.source_en: What Hideyoshi had said of him at Hidenaga’s residence, how Hidenaga had brought in his daughter and then withdrawn—all of it gradually faded from his mind.

paragraphs.source_en: He spent the next two days in Osaka and returned to the capital on the thirtieth. At the Jurakudai in Uchino, Ieyasu’s lodgings had been completed; Tōdō Takatora and the others, who had labored day and night, already had everything prepared. That night, Ieyasu, Tōdō Takatora, Sakai Tadatsugu, and Sakakibara Yasumasa were seated together. Hideyoshi once again brought up Shintarō.

If he truly became Hidenaga’s son-in-law, the people of Okazaki and Hamamatsu would surely regard him as a traitor. How would his lord answer? As Shintarō pondered this, his heart kept pounding.

paragraphs.source_en: From the moment Yasumasa went to fetch his father, Shintarō sensed that the matter had become troublesome and held his breath. If Hideyoshi could simply take the sons of the Tokugawa family’s hereditary retainers one after another whenever they pleased him, the Tokugawa house would soon be hollowed out. Might the day come when Shintarō could be neither Hideyoshi’s vassal nor a Tokugawa vassal?

paragraphs.source_en: For a long while, Shintarō heard nothing of what the others were saying. His lord was well satisfied, and Hideyoshi was exceedingly pleased. It would be a terrible omen if this affair damaged the goodwill between them.
